paper.title: Tracking Most Significant Shifts in Nonparametric Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Non-stationary Lipschitz (nonparametric) contextual bandits, experienced significant shifts
unmapped: Contexts in [0,1]^d; mean reward functions f_t^a are 1-Lipschitz in the context (sup norm) for every t
Strong density assumption on the (fixed) context marginal
Oblivious adversary picks a sequence of independent joint distributions D_t of (context, rewards)
Non-stationarity measured by number of experienced significant shifts (locally counted best-arm changes at observed contexts), unknown to learner
settings.definition_quote: an oblivious adversary decides a sequence of (independent) distributions on $\{(X_t,Y_t)\}_{t\in[T]}$ before the first round. ... R_T(\pi,\bld{X}_T) \doteq \sum_{t = 1}^{T} \max_{a \in [K]} f_t^a(X_t) -  f_t^{\pi_t}(X_t)

settings.name_in_paper: Non-stationary Lipschitz contextual bandits, total variation V_T
unmapped: Contexts in [0,1]^d; mean reward functions 1-Lipschitz in the context
Strong density assumption on context marginal
Total variation V_T = sum_t ||D_t - D_{t-1}||_TV of joint distributions, unknown to learner
settings.definition_quote: Define $V_T \doteq \sum_{t=2}^T \|\mc{D}_t - \mc{D}_{t-1}\|_{\text{TV}}$ where recall $\mc{D}_t \in \mc{X}\times [0,1]^K$ is the joint distribution on context and rewards at time $t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Non-stationary Lipschitz contextual bandits with at most L global shifts or total variation at most V (lower bound)
unmapped: Contexts uniform on [0,1]^d; mean rewards 1-Lipschitz in context
Family of environments with either total variation <= V or at most L global shifts (union of switching and drifting classes)
settings.definition_quote: For $V, L\in [0,T]$, let $\mc{P}(V,L,T)$ be the family of joint distributions $\mc{D} \doteq \{\mc{D}_t\}_{t\in [T]}$ with either total variation $V_T \leq V$ or at most $L$ global shifts.

algorithms.name: Oracle procedure (successive elimination restarted at experienced significant shifts)

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Suppose there are $K=2$ arms. For $V, L\in [0,T]$, let $\mc{P}(V,L,T)$ be the family of joint distributions ... with either total variation $V_T \leq V$ or at most $L$ global shifts. Then, there exists a constant $c>0$ such that for any policy $\pi$: \sup_{\mc{D} \in \mc{P}(V,L,T)} \mb{E}_{\mc{D}}[R(\pi,\bld{X}_T)] \geq  c \left(T^{\frac{1+d}{2+d}} + T^{\frac{2+d}{3+d}}\cdot V^{\frac{1}{3+d}}\right) \land \left(  (L+1)^{\frac{1}{2+d}} T^{\frac{1+d}{2+d}} \right).

results.notes: L (global shifts) mapped to S_T, V (TV budget) to V_T. The sup is over a union family (either TV<=V or <=L shifts), recorded under the switching setting.

symbols.Phi_sig: sum over experienced significant phases i of (tau_{i+1}-tau_i)^((1+d)/(2+d))

conditions: oracle knows the experienced significant shift times tau_i
Lipschitz rewards and strong density assumption

source.label: prop:sanity
source.quote: We have the oracle procedure $\pi$ of \Cref{defn:oracle} satisfies with probability at least $1-1/T^2$ w.r.t. the randomness of $\bld{X}_T$: for some $C>0$ \mb{E}_{\pi}[ R_T(\pi,\bld{X}_T) \mid \bld{X}_T ] \leq C\log(K) \log(T) \sum_{i=0}^{\tilde{L}(\bld{X}_T)} (\tau_{i+1}-\tau_{i})^{\frac{1+d}{2+d}}\cdot K^{\frac{1}{2+d}}.

results.notes: Bound on conditional expected dynamic regret given contexts, holding w.p. >= 1-1/T^2 over contexts. Oracle uses shift times (not in vocabulary).

symbols.Phi_sig: sum over experienced significant phases of (phase length)^((1+d)/(2+d))

conditions: Lipschitz rewards and strong density assumption
experienced significant shifts unknown to learner

source.label: thm
source.quote: Let $\{\tau_i(\bld{X}_T)\}_{i =0}^{\tilde L+1}$ denote the unknown experienced significant shifts. We then have w.p. at least $1-1/T^2$ w.r.t. the randomness of $\bld{X}_T$, for some $C>0$: \mb{E}[ R_T(\cmeta,\bld{X}_T) \mid \bld{X}_T] \leq C \log(K)\log^{3}(T) \sum_{i=1}^{\Lsig(\bld{X}_T)} (\tau_{i}(\bld{X}_T) - \tau_{i-1}(\bld{X}_T))^{\frac{1+d}{2+d}}\cdot K^{\frac{1}{2+d}}.

results.notes: Conditional expected regret given contexts, w.h.p. over contexts. Requires T (removable with doubling).

symbols.L_sig: number of experienced significant shifts (depends on the context sequence)

conditions: Lipschitz rewards and strong density assumption

source.label: cor:sig-shift-num
source.quote: Under the conditions of \Cref{thm}, with probability at least $1-1/T^2$ w.r.t. the randomness in $\bld{X}_T$: \mb{E}[ R_T(\cmeta,\bld{X}_T) \mid \bld{X}_T] \leq C\log(K) \log^{3}(T)\cdot (K\cdot ( \Lsig(\bld{X}_T)+1))^{\frac{1}{2+d}}\cdot T^{\frac{1+d}{2+d}}.

conditions: Lipschitz rewards and strong density assumption

source.label: cor:tv
source.quote: Under the conditions of \Cref{thm}: \mb{E}[ R_T(\cmeta,\bld{X}_T) ] \leq C\log(K) \log^{3}(T) \left( T^{\frac{1+d}{2+d}}\cdot K^{\frac{1}{2+d}} + (V_T\cdot K)^{\frac{1}{3+d}}\cdot T^{\frac{2+d}{3+d}} \right).

results.notes: Expectation over contexts, rewards and algorithm randomness.

conditions: environment drawn uniformly from a finite family of stationary Lipschitz environments
algorithm may use extra independent randomness U

source.label: prop:stationary-lower
source.quote: Suppose there are $K=2$ arms. Then, there exists a finite family of stationary Lipschitz contextual bandit environments $\mc{E}(n)$ over $n$ rounds such that for any algorithm $\pi$ taking as input random variable $U$, we have for some constant $c>0$ ... \mb{E}_{\mc{E}\sim \Unif(\mc{E}(n)),U}[ R(\pi,\bld{X}_T)] \geq c\cdot n^{\frac{1+d}{2+d}}.

results.notes: n is the horizon. Construction follows Rigollet & Zeevi without margin parameter.
